name: IT team · M2 — workspace preview through Traefik (deployable + demoable)
description:
Milestone M2 — a workspace app is served at its own URL through the proxy and its preview is visible from the platform UI.

IN SCOPE
- Workspace routing through Traefik for one workspace, end to end.
- Preview renders the real application inside the platform (or its live URL is copyable from the UI).

DEMO (5 min, management)
open the platform → open the workspace → the preview renders the real app → the workspace URL can be opened in a second tab.

DEPLOYABLE: yes — one workspace, flagged/limited.
DEPENDS ON: M1 (stack up) and the Traefik routing table being generated; if a route is missing, capture `traefik routes` output before changing anything.
NOT IN THIS INCREMENT: several workspaces at once, custom domains, TLS for workspace domains.

DEFINITION OF DONE: route table captured in a comment, preview proven with a real workspace, QA gate not `block`, demo script written.

OWNER: devops (Traefik/routes) · workspace (workspace bring-up).
DATE: 2026-11-25 — FORECAST until the owner confirms.

ACCEPTANCE: a comment with the merged Traefik route used, the working workspace URL, and how the preview was verified.

open the platform → open the workspace → the preview renders the real app → the workspace URL can be opened in a second tab.

DEPLOYABLE: yes — one workspace, flagged/limited.
DEPENDS ON: M1 (stack up) and the Traefik routing table being generated; if a route is missing, capture `traefik routes` output before changing anything.
NOT IN THIS INCREMENT: several workspaces at once, custom domains, TLS for workspace domains.

DEFINITION OF DONE: route table captured in a comment, preview proven with a real workspace, QA gate not `block`, demo script written.

OWNER: devops (Traefik/routes) · workspace (workspace bring-up).
DATE: 2026-11-25 — FORECAST until the owner confirms.

ACCEPTANCE: a comment with the merged Traefik route used, the working workspace URL, and how the preview was verified.

QA shift 2026-11-18 — the same clarification as on M1: "QA gate not `block`" is currently un-satisfiable (empty `qa_policy.suites` + `api/` not indexed from the QA seat), and it is **not** a Traefik defect. Do not treat it as a reason to stop the routing work.

What QA will accept as evidence for M2:
1. The **merged** Traefik route, pasted (router rule + service + entrypoint), and the command that produced it.
2. `curl -sS -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}\n' <workspace URL>` → `200`, plus one line of the response body proving it is the real app and not the platform shell (e.g. its `<title>`).
3. The preview inside the platform: screenshot of the workspace opened in the UI **and** the same URL opened in a second tab.
4. The negative case, because a router that matches everything looks identical to a correct one: one URL that must **not** resolve to the workspace (another workspace, or the platform itself) and its actual status code.

Point 4 is the one that distinguishes "preview works" from "preview works for one workspace only" — please include it in the acceptance comment.

**Manager note on M2 — read before you wake on 23 Nov 09:00.**

1. **You are not blocked by M1.** `b9aaf03c` (M1, one-command demo bring-up) is a separate infrastructure slice with its own demo on 21 Nov. If M1 slips, you still start on 23 Nov: you build the Traefik workspace preview on whatever bring-up exists. Do not wait for M1 to be marked `Done`.

2. **M1's demo is your first backlog input, not a gate.** Whatever management re-orders on 21 Nov comes back as a change to *your* scope. If it changes what you build, it changes your date or your scope — say which, on this card, and tell me. Do not absorb a scope change silently.

3. **Deployable + demoable is the bar.** By end of day 25 Nov the card must be demonstrable in 5 minutes: open a workspace in the browser, served through Traefik, websocket connected. If the websocket/headers part is not finished, ship the preview behind a flag and put the missing piece in a follow-up card — a working preview that is demoed beats a complete one that is not.

4. **Owner split stays as written:** `devops` owns the routing/compose wiring, `workspace` owns the preview behaviour in the UI. If you need a test written to close the QA gate, that is card `5ee9dbfa` — do not write a test just to make a gate pass.

Report in the shift format: on track / at risk / off track in the first line, with the demo evidence (URL, command output, or screenshot reference).

**Manager ruling on M2 — read this before you wake on 23 Nov 09:00.**

Three corrections, so you do not wake into criteria you cannot meet.

**1. The DoD line "QA gate not `block`" is struck — do not treat it as a blocker on your work.**
It is un-satisfiable today and it is not a Traefik defect. The gate returns `block` only because `qa_policy.suites` is empty (card `d1ba037a`) and the source→test map is missing (card `5ee9dbfa`). Both are owned elsewhere and both are armed. Replacing that line:

> **Amended DoD:** route table captured in a comment · preview proven with a real workspace · demo script present on this card · **a gate `block` is *attributed* on this card in one line** (name the missing suite/test), never silently worked around.
>
> This is exactly the ruling already applied to M1 (`b9aaf03c`) on 18 Nov. QA's comment of 18 Nov on this card already lists what it will accept as evidence, so QA and management now agree in writing. Do not re-open it.

**2. The acceptance bar is the one in the card description, not the wording in my earlier note.** The note said "websocket connected"; the description says "preview renders the real application inside the platform (or its live URL is copyable from the UI)". Resolved as follows:
- **Required (the bar):** (a) the **merged** Traefik route pasted — router rule + service + entrypoint — with the command that produced it; (b) `curl -sS -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}\n' <workspace URL>` → `200`, plus one line of the body proving it is the real app and not the platform shell; (c) the preview visible in the UI **and** the same URL opened in a second tab; (d) the **negative case** QA asked for — one URL that must *not* resolve to the workspace, with its actual status code.
- **Not the bar: websocket.** If the websocket does not connect cleanly, ship the preview **behind a flag**, demo points (a)–(d), and open a follow-up card for the websocket. A working preview that is demoed beats a complete one that is not. Do not let it hold the milestone.

**3. Your demo script arrives on this card on 22 Nov 09:00**, from card `fe9f284d`, written in the M1 format so management can diff two demos. It is written **after** the 21 Nov outcome card `70832a68`, so if management re-orders M2 scope on Friday the script demos the re-ordered scope. You do not write it and you are not blocked waiting for it.

**Date:** 25 Nov stays a **FREECAST** — I am not calling it a commitment. It becomes a commitment when you paste the route evidence in (a). If the websocket work or the negative case pushes it, say so on this card with the number of days, and I will re-forecast rather than absorb it silently.

**Owners unchanged:** `devops` owns routing/compose wiring · `workspace` owns the preview behaviour in the UI. One owner per deliverable — if a piece is unowned, it does not exist.

**Correction to the ruling above (typo, one word):** point 3 reads "**FREECAST**" — it should read "**FORECAST**". The meaning of the sentence is unchanged and is the intended one: 25 Nov is a **forecast, not a commitment**, until you paste the merged-route evidence. Nothing else in the ruling changes.

## PM ruling (shift #7, turn 4) — your start time is correct under Option A and **wrong under Option B**. Do not change the date; read the branch below.

You wake **Mon 23 Nov 09:00Z**. Under the current default (demo stays **Sat 21 Nov 13:00Z**) that is correct and clean: the demo happened, `70832a68` re-forecasts at 08:00Z, you build against the re-ordered scope.

**But if `2506f948` recorded Option B, the M1 demo moves to Mon 23 Nov 13:00Z — four hours *after* you wake.** Your own instruction says *"if the M1 demo re-ordered the scope, the script demos the re-ordered scope"*. Under Option B no scope has been re-ordered yet when you start, and the first increment of M2 would be built against a plan management has not yet seen. That violates the one rule that outranks tidier scheduling: **demo before planning the next increment.**

### The branch, decided by a fact you can read
Read the last comment on `2506f948` before your first action.

- **Recorded Option A** → proceed normally, all of M2 in scope.
- **Recorded Option B** → you may do **read-only preparation only** until the demo outcome is written on `70832a68`: capture the current Traefik route table, the existing routers/services, compose wiring, and paste it in a comment. **Do not change a route, a compose file or entrypoint, and do not write the demo script.** When the outcome comment exists, continue.
- **No answer recorded** → treat as Option A. Silence moves nothing; that is the standing rule from `2506f948`.

### Two things about your card that are correct and must not change
- **One owner per deliverable:** `devops` (routes/compose) · `workspace` (preview behaviour in the UI). Do not let a piece become unowned.
- **25 Nov is a FORECAST, not a commitment** — it becomes a commitment only when the merged-route evidence is pasted. (Your earlier "FREECAST" typo is already corrected; the meaning stands.)

### Standing constraint
`demo/` is frozen from **20 Nov 17:30Z** for the M1 security gate. M2 does not need to touch it; if you believe it must, that is a PM decision, not a card decision — say so and wait.
